page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The major constituents
lines: Portland cement is a mixture of oxides.
steps.why: Lime, silica and alumina together make up between three quarters and nine tenths of the cement, and they are the oxides that react with water when the cement sets. Each one is written with its formula and its percentage range.
common_mistakes: Writing 55% for CaO or 22% for SiO₂. The question asks for an average composition, so each oxide is written as the range it lies in.
Writing Ca₂O or CaO₂ for lime. Calcium oxide is CaO.
steps.memory_tip: Lime is the largest share, then silica, then alumina.
steps.margin_note: Write the formula and the percentage range together for each oxide.

steps.label: The smaller amounts
lines: The remaining oxides are present in
For good cement the SiO₂ : Al₂O₃ ratio
steps.why: The three small oxides complete the list of six. The silica to alumina ratio is the quality check applied to a sample, so it is worth adding once the list is finished.
common_mistakes: Stopping at five oxides. SO₃ belongs in the list, and without it the composition is short of one of the six.
Writing Fe₃O₄ or FeO for the iron oxide. The one reported in cement is ferric oxide, Fe₂O₃.
steps.memory_tip: Six oxides in all: three large amounts, three small ones.
steps.margin_note: Finish the list of six oxides before adding the quality ratio.

insider_note: The whole answer is a list, so write all six oxides with their formulae and ranges instead of describing cement in words.
